reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1200-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-06), driven primarily by a defect in the billing calculation/import-validation step that produces incorrect bills even when the underlying meter read was correctly recorded as ACTUAL: disputed bills skew toward ACTUAL (1785) over ESTIMATED (1240) reads (E-01), ruling out estimate-substitution (AMI or field read gaps) as the primary driver. No tariff change occurred this year (E-03, E-04) and ticket response times remain within SLA (E-05), so neither tariff shifts nor slow handling explain the surge; degraded manual-read route completion (0.88 vs 0.95 target, 9200 accounts, E-02) is at most a secondary contributor.
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1200-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-06), with onset coinciding with billing-import rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01), which compares raw AMI register values against 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling (E-13). Because firmware v4.2 meters (rollout June 2026) report reads in 0.1 m3 sub-units rather than whole m3 (E-14), legitimate high-usage v4.2 reads are misclassified as anomalous: AMI read events for the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills show 1184 rejected at import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION and 56 with no accepted read, driving estimate-substitution disputes for that bucket (E-12).
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
